verdict.rationale: The README is served from the public dagster-io/dagster GitHub repository, so the product's source is publicly readable. The docs also include an 'oss' deployment section, which suggests an open-source edition. However, no evidence names the license or confirms its terms. Missing for 10: explicit statement of an open-source license (e.g., Apache-2.0), first-party licensing docs, and independent corroboration of open-source status.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can read the product's source under an open license

citations.quote: With Dagster, you declare—as Python functions—the data assets that you want to build. Dagster then helps you run your functions at the right time and keep your assets up-to-date.
A typical Dagster Docker deployment includes a several long-running containers: one for the webserver, one for the daemon, and one for each code location.
